What Home Affairs Confirms About Evidence Levels

Australia's Student visa (subclass 500) uses an Evidence Level, formerly called an assessment level, of one, two or three. It is set using your passport country and your education provider together. The Department of Home Affairs does not publish the level of any country or provider, and it updates the levels twice a year, in March and September. Study Australia says the latest update took effect on September 30, 2026.

Agents have reported that Nepal has been treated as Level 3, the highest level, since January 2026, and that refusals for Nepali applicants rose. We could not confirm either point from an official source, and no official refusal rate for Nepal is published. So this guide does not tell you your level. It explains what to prepare, whichever level applies to you.

📋
What are Evidence Levels? Study Australia says Evidence Levels guide the financial and English evidence a Student visa applicant must provide. They do not affect visa eligibility or priority processing, and every application is assessed on its own merits. Even where a document is not required at lodgement, you may be asked for it during processing, so prepare everything upfront. To see what applies to your passport and provider, use the Document Checklist Tool on the Home Affairs website.

For the rule changes that started on October 2, 2026, read our guide to the Australia Student visa changes from October 2, 2026. For the destination overview, see Study in Australia from Nepal.

Confirmed vs Reported: Nepal and Level 3

Many pages state Nepal's level as fact. We separate what an official source says from what agents say, so you know how much weight to give each point.

What Funds Do You Need to Show?

Study Australia says international student visa applicants must show at least AUD 29,710 for living costs, and warns that real costs depend on the city and can be much higher. The tuition and other parts of the calculation depend on your course, so check the Home Affairs financial capacity page. Our guide to the Australia Student visa fee, funds and OSHC covers the figures in detail.

Home Affairs does not publish a single rule on how long money must sit in an account. The points below are good practice for any level, not official requirements:

  • Keep a clear paper trail: Be ready to show where the money comes from, such as salary slips, business tax records or documents for the sale of a property. Savings and liquid funds are easier to prove than asset valuations.
  • Avoid unexplained large deposits: A sudden deposit just before you apply invites questions. If a large sum arrives, keep the document that explains it.
  • Check your education loan letter: If you use a loan, make sure the sanction letter states what it covers (tuition, living costs or both) and that the lender is a recognized bank.
  • Leave a margin: Do not plan to hit the minimum exactly. Costs and exchange rates move.
⚠️
Start preparing months ahead Finance documents take time to gather. Begin well before your intended lodgement date, and lodge early enough to leave room for processing. Home Affairs publishes processing times, so check the current figures instead of relying on an agent's estimate.

The Genuine Student Statement

The Genuine Student (GS) requirement applies to Student visa applications lodged on or after March 23, 2024. The application asks about your circumstances, including ties to family, community, employment and finances, and you explain why you chose your course and Australia, and how the course benefits you. Study Australia gives no pass mark or scoring method, so write honest, specific answers about your own plans.

Cover these four things clearly:

  • Why this course? Explain the link between your academic or work background and the course. A computing graduate applying for an IT master's has a clear story. An unrelated course needs a convincing reason.
  • Why Australia and this provider? Refer to specific features of the course or provider, not general praise of Australian universities.
  • What are your plans after the course? Keep them realistic and connected to what you study.
  • What ties do you have to Nepal? Family, work, community and financial circumstances all belong in your answer.
✍️
Keep your SOP and GS answers consistent The SOP goes to your provider and the GS answers go to Home Affairs. They are written for different readers, but they should tell the same story about your goals and your reasons for choosing Australia. Write them together, not separately. Copied or template answers do not show your real situation.

English Test Scores for the Student Visa

For a standard application with no ELICOS or foundation study attached, the minimums in the Home Affairs instrument are IELTS Academic 6.0 (average band), PTE Academic 47 and TOEFL iBT 67. Lower minimums apply when your course includes at least 10 or 20 weeks of ELICOS or an eligible foundation or pathway program. Your provider can also ask for a higher score than the visa minimum, so use the higher of the two.

  • Take the test at a test center: At-home or online tests are not accepted.
  • Check validity: Scores are generally valid for 24 months before you apply.
  • Check exemptions: Home Affairs lists some cases where no test is needed. The Document Checklist Tool shows what applies to you.

The full score table, with all nine approved tests, is in our guide to IELTS, PTE or TOEFL minimum scores for the Australia Student visa. If you are weighing options, see studying in Australia without IELTS.

Why Your Provider Matters

Because the Evidence Level uses your passport country and your education provider together, your choice of provider can change which documents you attach. Home Affairs does not publish provider levels either, so ask each provider directly, and run the Document Checklist Tool for the course you plan to apply for.

  • Ask the provider in writing: Ask which documents students from Nepal are usually asked to attach for your course.
  • Compare more than one option: Run the checklist tool for two or three providers and compare the document lists.
  • Check the provider's CRICOS registration: You need a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) from a registered provider.

How to Prepare a Complete Application: Step by Step

  1. Choose your course and provider early Pick a course with a clear link to your background. Allow several months before your intake for offers, the CoE and your finance documents.
  2. Run the Document Checklist Tool Enter your passport and the provider and course. Save the result and use it as your checklist.
  3. Organize your finance documents Gather statements, source-of-funds documents and any loan letter. Keep an explanation ready for any large deposit.
  4. Book your English test early Aim for a margin above the minimum so a retake is not needed. Check your provider's own requirement as well.
  5. Write your SOP and GS answers together Keep your goals, your reasons for choosing Australia and your ties to Nepal consistent across both.
  6. Lodge a complete application Attach every document the tool shows and lodge in good time before your course start date.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Nepal Evidence Level 3 for the Australia Student visa?
Home Affairs does not publish the Evidence Level of any country, so we cannot confirm it. Agents have reported Nepal at Level 3 since January 2026, but that is unconfirmed. Use the Document Checklist Tool on the Home Affairs website to see which documents apply to your passport and provider.
Does a higher Evidence Level mean my visa will be refused?
No. Study Australia says Evidence Levels guide the finance and English evidence you attach. They do not affect visa eligibility or priority processing, and every application is assessed on its own merits.
How much money must I show for an Australian Student visa?
Study Australia says applicants must show at least AUD 29,710 for living costs, and real costs can be higher depending on the city. The tuition and other parts of the calculation depend on your course, so check the Home Affairs financial capacity page. See our guide to the visa fee, funds and OSHC for details.
What is the Genuine Student requirement?
It applies to Student visa applications lodged on or after March 23, 2024. You explain why you chose your course and Australia, how the course benefits you, and your circumstances, including ties to family, community, employment and finances. Study Australia gives no pass mark, so write specific, honest answers.
What English score do I need for the Australia Student visa?
For a standard application, the Home Affairs minimums are IELTS Academic 6.0, PTE Academic 47 and TOEFL iBT 67. Lower minimums apply with ELICOS or foundation study, and your provider can ask for more. See our English test guide for the full table.
